newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Greenspan wave seen pushing Russian shares up more.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan wave seen pushing Russian shares up more.

text.p: Russian and foreign investors caught U.S. Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's positive attitude and pushed prices of leading Russian shares up in the sharpest uptick in three weeks, traders said on Wednesday.
They predicted enthusiasm was strong enough to keep prices rising on Thursday but declined to make longer term forecasts.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index rose 4.32 percent to 492.60 on $76.54 million market turnover, almost double the Tuesday's $41.60 million.

Shares of national power utility UES EESR.RTS, which President Boris Yeltsin authorised to issue convertible bonds, rose to $0.4320 from $0.4174 and Nizhnevartovskneftegaz NZGZ.RTS rose to $24.00 from $21.50. Traders said non-portfolio investors were interested in the oil company.
"When we saw the Dow Jones over 8,000, it was tough to believe the market would do anything else," Raiffeisenbank Austria equity chief Sergei Sheikov said of the bullish day.
"A big part of that was Greenspan, but note that there is also interest in Russia."

Federal Reserve Chairman Greenspan gave a generally perceived upbeat view of the U.S. economy to Congress on Tuesday and Wednesday, propelling the Dow Jones over 8,000, although profit-taking ate up some of the gains on Wednesday.
Sheikov said demand was chiefly from short-term speculators but strong enough to move shares up on Thursday.
Renaissance Capital trader Vladimir Chkhikvadze said there was a new wave of investment but was wary of saying whether the growth would be more than short-term.
